question: Find all employees in the Engineering department
Get the average salary per department
answer: SELECT dept, AVG(salary) as avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY dept

schema: orders(id, customer_id, amount, status, created_at), customers(id, name, email)
question: Find customers who have never placed an order
answer: SELECT c.* FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.id IS NULL

question: Get top 5 most expensive products
answer: SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5

schema: orders(id, customer_id, amount, status), order_items(order_id, product_id, qty, price)
question: Get total revenue per order
answer: SELECT o.id, SUM(oi.qty * oi.price) as revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.id

question: Find employees who earn more than their department average
answer: SELECT e.* FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees WHERE dept = e.dept)

question: Count products with zero stock per category
answer: SELECT category, COUNT(*) as out_of_stock FROM products WHERE stock = 0 GROUP BY category

schema: users(id, name, created_at), sessions(id, user_id, duration_mins, created_at)
question: Find users with average session duration over 30 minutes
answer: SELECT u.name, AVG(s.duration_mins) as avg_duration FROM users u JOIN sessions s ON u.id = s.user_id GROUP BY u.id, u.name HAVING AVG(s.duration_mins) > 30

question: Get monthly sales totals for 2024
answer: SELECT MONTH(sale_date) as month, SUM(amount) as total FROM sales WHERE YEAR(sale_date) = 2024 GROUP BY MONTH(sale_date) ORDER BY month

question: Find the second highest salary
answer: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees)

schema: posts(id, user_id, title, created_at), likes(post_id, user_id)
question: Get top 3 most liked posts
answer: SELECT p.title, COUNT(l.user_id) as likes FROM posts p LEFT JOIN likes l ON p.id = l.post_id GROUP BY p.id, p.title ORDER BY likes DESC LIMIT 3
